questions.q: What are the three stages of this project's pipeline, in order?
options: T-SQL extract, Python clean/join, Power BI model and report
Excel, Power Query, Power BI
Power BI, Python, T-SQL
T-SQL, Power BI, Python
questions.explain: The pipeline runs T-SQL extraction first, then Python cleaning/joining, then Power BI modeling and reporting.

questions.q: Why does the extraction (filtering, joining, aggregating source tables) happen in T-SQL rather than pulling raw tables elsewhere first?
options: Power BI requires all data to already be pre-joined before Get Data
Python cannot connect to SQL Server at all
The database is faster at this and keeps the extract focused on exactly what each question needs
T-SQL is the only language that can read AdventureWorks2012
questions.explain: Filtering and joining at the source is faster and keeps the extract scoped to what's actually needed.

questions.q: Why does the cross-extract cleaning and joining happen in Python instead of only in Power Query?
options: Power Query cannot merge two tables under any circumstances
T-SQL cannot produce two separate result sets
It's repeatable, inspectable, re-runnable code — exactly what pandas functions like merge, dropna, and drop_duplicates are built for
Python is required by Power BI for all data loading
questions.explain: This project deliberately builds the Python cleaning/joining skill rather than relying only on manual Power Query clicks.

questions.q: What does Stage 3 (Power BI) take as its input?
options: Two separate Power BI files, one per stakeholder
The two raw T-SQL extracts, unmodified
A direct live connection to AdventureWorks2012 with no prior stages
One clean, combined dataset produced by the Python stage
questions.explain: Power BI builds its model and both report pages on the single combined dataset Python produces.

questions.q: Why plan the pipeline in plain English before writing any code?
options: T-SQL cannot be written without a prior Python script
It clarifies what each stage takes in and produces before implementation decisions get made
Plain-English planning is a Power BI technical requirement
It replaces the need for a data model entirely
questions.explain: Planning the inputs and outputs of each stage up front avoids guessing mid-build.
